extension.description: Records your spec-kit runs live: status, resume, and a health check for what actually happened.
extension.author: alfredoperez

pageProps.readmeContent:
SpecKit Companion: the Spec Kit extension

This extension runs inside [Spec Kit](https://github.com/github/spec-kit) and records every step of a run in `.spec-context.json`, a plain file beside each spec. That record is what gives you live progress, a resume command and the Overview of a run, in your terminal and in every [SpecKit Companion](https://speckit-companion.dev) surface. ## Requirements - A Spec Kit CLI installed from GitHub. The PyPI `specify-cli` has no `extension` command. - `python3` is optional. Without it the recording is skipped and your Spec Kit command still runs. ```bash uv tool install specify-cli --from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git --force ``` ## Install, update and verify From your project root: ```bash specify extension add companion --from https://github.com/alfredoperez/speckit-companion/releases/download/companion-latest/companion.zip --force ``` Run the same line again to update, because that URL always serves the newest build. To verify, run `specify extension list` and look for `companion`. Then run `/speckit.specify` once and check that `specs//.spec-context.json` was written. More in [docs/install.md](./docs/install.md). ## First run You don't have to change how you work. The extension hooks into the stock `/speckit.*` commands and records them as they run. To use Companion's own pipeline, which writes shorter specs and sizes itself to the change, start a spec in your assistant: ```text /speckit.companion.specify "let users upload a profile photo" ``` Then run plan, tasks and implement the same way, or all four at once with `/speckit.companion.auto`. At any point `/speckit.companion.status` prints where the spec stands and `/speckit.companion.resume` continues from there. ## Commands | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `/speckit.companion.specify` | Write the spec and size the change | | `/speckit.companion.plan` | Write `plan.md` | | `/speckit.companion.tasks` | Write `tasks.md`, ordered by dependency | | `/speckit.companion.implement` | Run the tasks, recording each one | | `/speckit.companion.auto` | Run the whole pipeline without pausing | | `/speckit.companion.status` | Print the current step, the decisions and the next action | | `/speckit.companion.resume` | Continue from the recorded step | | `/speckit.companion.doctor` | Report on a run's health. Read-only | | `/speckit.companion.living-adopt` | Draft living specs for existing code | | `/speckit.companion.living-sync` | Update living specs from your current changes | | `/speckit.companion.living-drift` | List files changed since a living spec was committed | | `/speckit.companion.living-coverage` | Show which requirements have a test | | `/speckit.companion.living-show` | Print one slice of a living spec | | `/speckit.companion.living-validate` | Check the shape of every living spec | | `/speckit.companion.living-move` | Move a living spec between central and colocated storage | The rest run by themselves, so don't type them: `speckit.companion.classify`, `speckit.companion.mark-complete`, and the hooks `speckit.companion.before-step`, `speckit.companion.after-specify`, `speckit.companion.after-plan`, `speckit.companion.after-tasks`, `speckit.companion.after-implement`, `speckit.companion.before-converge` and `speckit.companion.after-converge`. Full reference: [docs/commands.md](./docs/commands.md). A build check requires every command to be named in this section. ## See it The record is a file, and the VS Code extension turns it into a page. Install it with `code --install-extension alfredoperez.speckit-companion`. ![The record a run leaves behind: the whole Overview page, per-phase timing, verified checks with their commands, and requirement-to-test coverage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alfredoperez/speckit-companion/main/docs/screenshots/generated/overview-engine.gif) ## SpecKit Companion runs in four places | Where | What it is | Start here | |---|---|---| | VS Code | The extension: a sidebar, a spec viewer and the Overview of every run. | [Install](https://speckit-companion.dev/docs/install) | | Spec Kit | The engine half: records each step so every surface can show progress and resume. | [Install](https://speckit-companion.dev/docs/install) | | GitHub Copilot app | A live spec board in the app's side panel. | [Copilot app](https://speckit-companion.dev/docs/copilot-app) | | Claude Code | The followed spec's run above your prompt and in a pane. | [Claude Code](https://speckit-companion.dev/docs/claude-code) | ## Docs The guides are at [speckit-companion.dev/docs](https://speckit-companion.dev/docs). The reference for this extension is in [docs/](./docs/), and releases are in the [changelog](./CHANGELOG.md). ## License [MIT](./LICENSE) © alfredoperez. Independently maintained and not affiliated with the Spec Kit core team.
